alerts.title: Carbamazepine reduces DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir (DTG) levels by 30-70%. The patient is on carbamazepine and a DTG-based regimen (TLD). The patient's viral load is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This interaction is a likely cause of virologic failure. The clinician's plan does not address this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch from carbamazepine to valproic acid as per guidelines, or consider an ART regimen change.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity and hyponatremia
alerts.message: The patient has symptoms (nystagmus, ataxia, tremor) and a carbamazepine level of 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic range 4-12), indicating toxicity. Concurrent hyponatremia (sodium 128 mmol/L) is a known side effect of carbamazepine and can exacerbate neurological symptoms. The clinician's plan to reduce the dose and repeat the level is appropriate but should also address the hyponatremia.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose, monitor sodium, and manage hyponatremia as clinically indicated.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT without monitoring plan
alerts.message: The patient has an elevated ALT of 68 U/L. Guidelines note that liver enzyme elevations can be drug-related. Potential causes include sodium valproate, carbamazepine, or other factors. The clinician's current plan does not include monitoring or evaluating this abnormality.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate cause of elevated ALT and schedule follow-up liver function tests.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring frequency gap
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend routine viral load monitoring every 12 months for adults on ART. The patient's last suppressed viral load was 176 days ago (over 5 months). The new detectable result indicates a monitoring gap was not the issue, but the result triggers the need for enhanced adherence counseling and a repeat test in 3 months per standard algorithms.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence counseling and schedule a repeat viral load in 3 months.
